title: Flood-risk disclosure and insurance rules can expose a coverage gap while purchase, affordability, and recovery remain open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108012 review of flood insurance coverage and policy options
geography: United States properties exposed to flood risk, including properties inside and outside FEMA special flood hazard areas

observations.period: April 2026 coverage data and October 1, 2026 GAO review

denominator.unit: high-risk properties outside FEMA special flood hazard areas identified in GAO's analysis of First Street data

high_risk_uninsured.unit: percent of high-risk properties without National Flood Insurance Program coverage as of April 2026

nfip_policy_change.value: NFIP policies declined from 5.5 million in 2010 to 4.5 million in 2026; private policies accounted for 14 percent of all flood-insurance policies in 2025

mandatory_purchase_signal.value: an estimated 43 percent of properties in FEMA special flood hazard areas had flood insurance compared with 2 percent outside those areas
mandatory_purchase_signal.unit: reported coverage share by mapped-risk status

policy_options.value: incorporate all flood sources into purchase determinations, publish property-level risk information, require lender quotes and signed declinations before closing, increase and periodically adjust NFIP limits, provide means-based affordability assistance, and remove barriers to private coverage

open_congressional_actions.unit: open matters for congressional consideration concerning risk criteria, property-level information, lender quotes/disclosures, and NFIP coverage limits

recovery_conversion.unit: property-owner risk awareness, insurance quote, purchase, premium affordability, coverage adequacy, claim, rebuilding, household displacement, or recovery

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108012, based on NFIP and private-market policy data, First Street property-risk analysis, stakeholder discussions, community visits, and policy-option review. Coverage, mapping, mandatory-purchase signal, options, open actions, and post-flood outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage estimates use distinct data sources and property universes; high-risk properties outside FEMA special flood hazard areas are not the same as all high-risk properties. Coverage shares do not establish why owners lack insurance, whether policies are affordable or adequate, or what happens after a flood.
observations.subgroup: Property owners and households in flood-prone communities, including owners with federally backed mortgages outside mapped special flood hazard areas and households with limited resources or incomplete risk information.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some properties may have private coverage, self-insurance, low perceived exposure, or geographic and underwriting constraints; expanding mandatory purchase or disclosure can improve information without guaranteeing affordable or adequate coverage or successful recovery.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the coverage, mapping, market, stakeholder, and policy-option findings.
The GAO companion map explains the high-risk coverage gap and NFIP/private insurance context.

boundary: This record advances a bounded flood exposure-to-mapping, insurance, and policy-option route. It does not establish property-level purchase, premium affordability, coverage adequacy, claim payment, rebuilding, household displacement, recovery, or community legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and companion map are retained for reproduction.
